Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Reno NV
203 PM PST Wed Nov 25 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

* Near average temperatures and dry conditions are expected on
  Thanksgiving with increasing cloud cover through the day. 

* Warming continues through Friday, with temperatures 4-8 degrees
  above average and continued dry conditions.

* Rain and higher elevation snow return Sunday into Monday, with
  more impactful storms possible mid-week and next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION

A warming and drying trend returns over the Thanksgiving holiday
and into the start of the week as high pressure builds across the
western U.S. Expect light winds and strengthening valley inversions
each morning which may lead to poor ventilation and areas degraded
air quality in the lower valleys. 

While skies will be mostly cloudy beginning tonight through the 
weekend, afternoon temperatures will warm 4-8 degrees above 
average Friday afternoon with highs generally in the upper 50s to
lower 60s across W.Nevada with low to mid 50s for Sierra valleys.

Winds over the Sierra ridgetops will strengthen Friday night into
Saturday, with gusts of 50-60 mph. A second pulse of wind arrives
Sunday morning, ahead of the next storm system, which is expected
Sunday into Monday. That system begins a more active weather 
pattern that should last into next weekend.

The first system will be relatively warm with rain and snow 
chances beginning Sunday afternoon in the E.Sierra, with snow 
levels around 7500-8000 feet, lowering to near 7500 feet by Monday
morning. Snow impacts should be mostly limited to passes above 
7500 feet, where there is a 20% chance of up to 2 inches of 
accumulation. Anyone traveling as the holiday weekend ends should 
allow extra time, even if roads are only wet or slushy.

Expect an active weather pattern next week. There is increasing
potential for more impactful storms early to mid-week, with 
another storm by next weekend. The first system could impact the 
E.Sierra Tuesday and Wednesday with snow levels around 5,500-6,500
feet, followed by a potentially colder storm with lower snow 
levels by next weekend. Timing and precipitation amounts remain 
uncertain, but impacts should exceed the Sunday-Monday storm. 
Overall, plan for winter conditions if planning travel across the 
Sierra next week. Fuentes

.AVIATION...

KRNO Forecast: 

* VFR conditions with light surface winds and increasing high
  clouds overnight. 

Regional Outlook: 

* 20% chance of FZFG for KTRK and the Martis Valley tonight, with
  otherwise light winds and VFR conditions expected for all other
  Sierra and W.Nevada terminals. 
  
24-72 Hour Outlook: 

* Valley inversions may also lead to increased haze buildup mainly
  around KRNO,KCXP,KMEV each morning, with minor reductions in 
  slantwise visibility. A more active weather pattern is expected 
  by late weekend into much of next week. Fuentes
